What if SDG 7 is not only about closing the access gap, but about building clean, affordable energy systems that power the next generation of development?
 
That was the question I kept coming back to today while moderating Panel Discussion 3: Accelerating Progress Towards 2030 and Beyond during the webinar “Clean and Affordable Energy: Where do we stand? How to move forward?”, ahead of the SDG 7 review at the HLPF.
 
There is real momentum to build on. For the first time in history, universal electricity access is within reach. More than 90% of the global population now has access to basic electricity, and global investment in the energy transition reached a record US$2.3 trillion in 2025.
 
But the task ahead is changing. Geopolitical tensions are exposing the vulnerability of major energy routes, affecting around 20 million barrels of oil per day. AI and digitalisation are also increasing demand on energy systems. By 2030, data centres could consume more electricity than all but five countries, and enough water to meet the basic needs of 1.3 billion people in sub-Saharan Africa for a year.
 
The opportunity is to power digital transformation with clean, affordable and resilient energy systems while advancing a just energy transition for all.
 
I was joined by Divya Kottadiel from Sustainable Energy for All (SEforALL) , @Luis Manuera from UN Environment Programme , and Isaac Elizondo from UNIDO for a rich exchange on what acceleration must look like in practice.
 
For me, one message stood out clearly: access must move from connection alone to energy for development and opportunity. That means powering schools, hospitals, farms, digital services and livelihoods, while creating jobs, supporting local enterprises and closing the digital divide for the 2.2 billion people still offline.
 
Finance is central to making this possible. Global clean energy investment has reached around US$2 trillion annually, yet Africa attracts only US$30-40 billion, roughly 2% of global flows. Redirecting capital toward countries and communities with the greatest needs is one of the biggest opportunities for shared prosperity.
 
If we get SDG 7 right, we do more than expand access. We make energy cleaner, more affordable and more productive, strengthening resilience, enabling digital participation, jobs and a just transition.
